summary: Adds a 3.0.6 EQL v3 upgrade self-edge to @cipherstash/stack-prisma and re-emits the genesis baseline (20260601T0100_install_eql_v3_bundle) to bake eql-3.0.6 with a fifth no-SQL carrier op, so the shipped baseline migrationHash moves again (bad30c9b… → 2fdc7caf…). I verified that the baked 3.0.6 SQL differs from the 3.0.5 bundle only in the version stamp (version(), schema comment, one comment line), and that the baseline and the 3.0.6 edge bake identical bytes. Because the migrations land before @cipherstash/eql is bumped from 3.0.5 (bumped by a pending patch changeset), the main risk is release ordering: the lockstep test now accepts either EQL version, so stack-prisma could ship baking 3.0.6 next to a 3.0.5 runtime package. Existing 1.x databases now re-install the bundle twice in one migrate, each install starting with DROP SCHEMA eql_v3 CASCADE. The stale-vendored-directory hazard (db init refusal, silent no-op without migration plan) was already present at the base from the unpublished 3.0.5 re-emit, and this change carries it forward. Offline tests targeting each of these paths exist but I did not see them run. The new live-Postgres tests self-skip without DATABASE_URL, and I found no CI job that sets it for this suite.

behaviour_changes.description: New migration 20261002T0000_upgrade_eql_v3_3_0_6: a data-class self-edge that executes the full eql-3.0.6 install SQL (which opens with DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS eql_v3 CASCADE) and records invariant cipherstash:upgrade-eql-v3-bundle-3.0.6-v1. Postchecks: version()='3.0.6', schema comment '3.0.6', eql_v3.query_json exists.

The genesis baseline is re-emitted: its install op now bakes eql-3.0.6 (sha 9b6dab78…), all carrier postchecks compare against '3.0.6', and a fifth additive carrier op for the 3.0.6 invariant is added; migrationHash changes to 2fdc7caf…. These bytes are content-addressed and copied into consumer repos.

The control descriptor exposes five migrations and the head ref requires five invariants, so `migration plan` seeds a new directory and every database whose markers lack the 3.0.6 invariant must walk an extra edge (databases on 1.0.0/1.1.x walk 3.0.5 then 3.0.6, installing the bundle twice).

Release ordering inverted: migrations baking eql-3.0.6 land while the workspace @cipherstash/eql is still 3.0.5; the lockstep test's version marker is widened to accept 3.0.5 or 3.0.6 for one cycle, and the live byte-identity check is documented as red by construction until the eql bump merges.
README, shipped skill skills/stash-prisma/SKILL.md, changesets and DEVELOPING.md updated to describe the 3.0.6 baseline and the 1.1.x upgrade path.

failure_scenarios.title: stack-prisma ships baking eql-3.0.6 while its pinned @cipherstash/eql runtime stays 3.0.5
failure_scenarios.trigger: A Version Packages release publishes @cipherstash/stack-prisma (minor, from .changeset/eql-3-0-6-migration.md) without @cipherstash/eql moving to a 3.0.6 whose install SQL digest is exactly 9b6dab78…, e.g. the eql changeset is deferred, the eql publish fails, or another EQL SQL change lands before the bump.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The lockstep test only requires that the installed release's digest is baked by some migration (migration-v3.test.ts:312), which 3.0.5 still satisfies through the 3.0.5 edge, and the version marker now accepts '3.0.5' or '3.0.6' (line 330). So CI stays green with stack-prisma baking 3.0.6 against a 3.0.5 @cipherstash/eql. The `*` in workspace:* is rewritten to the exact eql version at pack time, and eql is not in stack-prisma's fixed changeset group (.changeset/config.json).
failure_scenarios.consequence: Databases migrated by prisma-next report eql-3.0.6, while `stash eql install` and other tools pinned through @cipherstash/eql install or expect 3.0.5. Version-based diagnostics disagree, and the shipped migrations reference an EQL release that may not exist on npm. Function behaviour is identical (verified stamp-only diff), so there is no data or ciphertext effect.

failure_scenarios.mitigation: Release the stack-prisma changeset only in the same Version Packages PR that bumps @cipherstash/eql to 3.0.6. Before publishing, confirm that the built eql package's installSqlSha256 equals 9b6dab78…. Narrow the version marker to '3.0.6' right after that merge, and consider adding a release gate that the baseline's baked digest equals the installed releaseManifest.

failure_scenarios.title: A version-stamp-only release re-runs DROP SCHEMA eql_v3 CASCADE on existing databases
failure_scenarios.trigger: `prisma-next plan` + `migrate` against an existing database whose markers lack the 3.0.6 invariant: every 1.0.0/1.1.x database (walks 3.0.5 then 3.0.6), and any database already at 3.0.5 built from main.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The 3.0.6 edge executes the full install bundle (migration.ts:75), which drops and recreates the eql_v3 schema with CASCADE. For 1.x databases this runs a second full ~2.6 MB install in the same transaction as the 3.0.5 edge. For a database already at 3.0.5 it is a new destructive reinstall for a stamp-only change. Dependent functional indexes, views, RLS policies and grants on eql_v3 objects are dropped and not recreated by the migration.
failure_scenarios.consequence: After the upgrade, encrypted-column queries lose their functional indexes (slow queries) and RLS policies or grants that referenced eql_v3 are gone until the operator recreates them. A longer single transaction holds locks for longer. No ciphertext is altered, because the public.eql_v3_* storage domains are preserved.

failure_scenarios.title: Temporarily widened lockstep marker and known-red live check outlive the release cycle
failure_scenarios.trigger: The follow-up to narrow the marker to '3.0.6' after the eql bump is forgotten, or the red live byte-identity check is ignored as expected noise.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: migration-v3.test.ts:330 accepts two versions, and migration-apply-live-pg.test.ts:168-171 is documented as failing by construction until the bump merges. Both rely on a manual follow-up.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Weaker guard against a future eql/stack-prisma pairing drift, or a live check that people learn to ignore. Detection is degraded, but nothing is directly broken.
missing_verification: No automated reminder or test that fails once @cipherstash/eql is 3.0.6 and the marker still lists 3.0.5
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Track the narrowing as a required follow-up in the Version Packages PR checklist.
